items.title: Hand Hygiene
items.description: A complete nursing guide to routine handwashing, alcohol-based hand rub, the WHO Five Moments, glove use and surgical hand preparation.
items.overview: Hand hygiene is one of the most important infection-prevention practices in healthcare. It includes cleaning the hands with soap and water, using an alcohol-based hand rub when appropriate, and surgical hand preparation before surgical procedures. For routine handwashing, the WHO procedure takes approximately 40–60 seconds. When hands are not visibly soiled, an alcohol-based hand rub is generally preferred for routine clinical hand hygiene.
items.why:
Why hand hygiene matters:
Hand hygiene helps reduce the transmission of microorganisms between healthcare workers, patients and the clinical environment.

WHO Five Moments:
1. Before touching a patient
2. Before a clean/aseptic procedure
3. After body fluid exposure risk
4. After touching a patient
5. After touching patient surroundings

Important: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Perform hand hygiene when clinically indicated before putting on gloves and after removing them.
equipment: Clean running water — for soap-and-water handwashing
Antimicrobial surgical hand preparation product — for surgical procedures
Sterile disposable towel — for surgical hand preparation
Sterile surgical gloves — after surgical hand preparation
Surgical gown, cap and mask — according to operating-room protocol
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Recognise the indication
steps.instruction: Identify when hand hygiene is required before beginning patient care.
steps.explanation: Use the WHO Five Moments as a framework: before touching a patient, before a clean or aseptic procedure, after body fluid exposure risk, after touching a patient and after touching patient surroundings.

steps.title: Prepare your hands
steps.instruction: Remove unnecessary hand and wrist jewellery and keep fingernails short and clean.
steps.explanation: Artificial nails and extensions should be avoided when caring for high-risk patients or when required by institutional policy. Check the hands for visible contamination.

steps.title: Wet the hands
steps.instruction: For soap-and-water handwashing, wet the hands with clean running water.
steps.explanation: Apply enough liquid soap to cover all surfaces of the hands.

steps.title: Rub palm to palm
steps.explanation: Create a lather and begin covering all surfaces of both hands.

steps.title: Clean the backs and between the fingers
steps.instruction: Rub the right palm over the left dorsum with fingers interlaced, then repeat on the opposite side.
steps.explanation: Continue by rubbing palm to palm with fingers interlaced so that the spaces between the fingers are cleaned.

steps.title: Clean the backs of the fingers
steps.instruction: Rub the backs of the fingers against the opposite palm with the fingers interlocked.
steps.explanation: This helps clean areas that are commonly missed during routine hand hygiene.

steps.title: Clean the thumbs and fingertips
steps.instruction: Rotationally rub each thumb and clean the fingertips and nail areas against the opposite palm.
steps.explanation: Pay particular attention to thumbs, fingertips, around and under the fingernails and other frequently missed areas.

steps.title: Clean the wrists
steps.instruction: Include the wrists when performing the handwashing procedure.
steps.explanation: Ensure all required hand surfaces have been cleaned before rinsing.

steps.title: Rinse and dry
steps.instruction: Rinse thoroughly with clean running water and dry completely with a single-use towel.
steps.explanation: For the WHO handwashing sequence, the entire procedure takes approximately 40–60 seconds.

steps.title: Turn off the faucet safely
steps.instruction: Use the disposable towel to turn off the faucet when appropriate.
steps.explanation: This helps avoid recontaminating clean hands by touching a potentially contaminated faucet handle.

steps.title: Alcohol-based hand rub
steps.instruction: When hands are not visibly soiled, use an appropriate alcohol-based hand rub according to the product instructions.
steps.explanation: Apply enough product to cover all hand surfaces. Rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, backs of fingers, thumbs and fingertips until the hands are completely dry. The CDC describes approximately 20 seconds for this process.

steps.title: Surgical hand preparation
steps.instruction: Before surgery, follow the approved surgical hand preparation method and the product manufacturer's instructions.
steps.explanation: Surgical hand preparation may use an antimicrobial soap-and-water method or an approved surgical alcohol-based hand preparation. Remove jewellery, keep nails short and clean, and follow the operating-room protocol for drying, gowning and sterile gloving. WHO guidance does not routinely recommend nail brushes because they can damage the skin.

steps.title: Hand hygiene and gloves
steps.instruction: Never use gloves as a substitute for hand hygiene.
steps.explanation: Perform hand hygiene whenever indicated before donning gloves and after removing gloves. Change gloves when required by the clinical situation, including when moving from a contaminated body site to a clean body site or between patients.

items.title: Blood Pressure Measurement
items.description: Understand the basic process of measuring blood pressure.
items.overview: Blood pressure measurement assesses the pressure of circulating blood against arterial walls.
items.why: Blood pressure is an important component of routine patient assessment.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Explain the procedure and prepare the appropriate equipment according to current clinical guidance.

steps.title: Position
steps.explanation: Use the position and arm placement required by your institution's current procedure.

steps.title: Measure
steps.explanation: Use the approved measurement technique for the equipment available.

steps.title: Record
steps.explanation: Document the measurement accurately according to local documentation requirements.

items.title: Temperature Measurement
items.description: Learn the basic principles of measuring body temperature.
items.overview: Temperature measurement provides an assessment of the body's temperature.
items.why: Temperature can contribute important information to a patient's overall assessment.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Select an appropriate measurement method and equipment according to current guidance.

steps.title: Position
steps.explanation: Use the technique appropriate to the device and measurement site.

steps.title: Measure
steps.explanation: Follow the manufacturer's instructions and local clinical procedure.

steps.title: Record
steps.explanation: Document the result and measurement method accurately.

items.title: Pulse Assessment
items.description: Learn the basic process of assessing a peripheral pulse.
items.overview: Pulse assessment involves evaluating the arterial pulse at an appropriate site.
items.why: Pulse assessment can provide useful information about cardiovascular status.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Prepare the patient and explain the assessment.
steps.explanation: Use an appropriate pulse site and follow your institution's assessment procedure.

steps.title: Locate
steps.explanation: Use the appropriate fingers and anatomical location according to clinical teaching.

steps.title: Assess
steps.explanation: Assess the characteristics required by your clinical procedure.

steps.title: Record
steps.explanation: Record the relevant assessment findings accurately.

items.title: Respiratory Rate Assessment
items.description: Learn how respiratory rate is assessed and documented.
items.overview: Respiratory rate is the number of breaths taken over a specified period.
items.why: Changes in breathing can provide important information about a patient's condition.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Observe
steps.explanation: Assess breathing discreetly and follow the appropriate clinical procedure.

steps.title: Count
steps.explanation: Use the timing method specified by your institution.

steps.title: Assess
steps.explanation: Follow your assessment framework for the characteristics that should be recorded.

steps.title: Record
steps.explanation: Record the result accurately and communicate concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

items.title: Bed Making
items.description: Learn the basic principles of preparing a clean patient bed.
items.overview: Bed making involves preparing a clean, safe and comfortable patient bed.
items.why: A properly prepared bed supports comfort, hygiene and patient safety.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Gather the required linen and follow local infection prevention procedures.

steps.title: Remove
steps.explanation: Handle used linen according to institutional infection-control procedures.

steps.title: Make
steps.explanation: Follow your nursing school's approved bed-making technique.

steps.title: Check
steps.explanation: Ensure the bed is clean, safe and appropriate for the patient's needs.

items.title: Oral Medication Administration
items.description: Explore the principles involved in oral medication administration.
items.overview: Oral medication administration involves giving medication by mouth according to an authorised prescription and clinical procedure.
items.why: Safe medication administration is a core nursing responsibility.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Verify
steps.instruction: Verify the medication order and patient.
steps.explanation: Follow your institution's medication safety checks and scope of practice.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Use the approved medication preparation process.

steps.title: Administer
steps.explanation: Follow the prescribed route, local policy and medication safety requirements.

steps.title: Document
steps.explanation: Record medication administration according to the applicable documentation system.

items.title: Intramuscular Injection
items.description: Learn the principles behind intramuscular medication administration.
items.overview: An intramuscular injection delivers medication into muscle tissue.
items.why: Intramuscular administration is one of several medication routes used in clinical practice.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Verify
steps.explanation: Complete the medication safety checks required by your institution.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Use an approved preparation and aseptic technique.

steps.title: Administer
steps.explanation: Injection site, needle selection and technique must follow current clinical guidance and patient-specific factors.

steps.title: Document
steps.explanation: Record the required details in the medication record.

items.title: Oxygen Therapy
items.description: Learn the basic nursing approach to safe oxygen therapy.
items.overview: Oxygen therapy provides supplemental oxygen when clinically indicated.
items.why: Correct oxygen delivery and monitoring support safe respiratory care.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Assess
steps.instruction: Assess the patient and oxygen requirement.
steps.explanation: Check the patient's respiratory status and follow the prescribed or local clinical guidance.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Select the appropriate device and check the equipment before use.

steps.title: Apply
steps.explanation: Position the device safely and provide the prescribed oxygen delivery.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.explanation: Reassess respiratory status and oxygen saturation and document findings.

items.title: Pulse Oximetry
items.description: Learn the basic process of obtaining and interpreting an SpO₂ reading.
items.overview: Pulse oximetry provides a non-invasive estimate of peripheral oxygen saturation.
items.why: SpO₂ can support assessment of a patient's respiratory status when used appropriately.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Explain the procedure and check that the device is ready for use.

steps.title: Position
steps.explanation: Use a suitable measurement site and ensure the sensor is positioned correctly.

steps.title: Read
steps.explanation: Assess the displayed value together with the patient's clinical condition.

steps.title: Record
steps.explanation: Record the reading and relevant clinical observations according to local requirements.

items.title: Capillary Blood Glucose
items.description: Learn the basic workflow for capillary blood glucose monitoring.
items.overview: Capillary blood glucose testing provides a point-of-care measurement of blood glucose.
items.why: Glucose monitoring can support assessment and management of patients with altered glucose levels.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Check the device, test strip and required infection-control supplies.

steps.title: Prepare Site
steps.instruction: Prepare the selected finger or approved site.
steps.explanation: Use the approved site-preparation technique for the device and local policy.

steps.title: Test
steps.instruction: Obtain and apply the blood sample.
steps.explanation: Use the manufacturer's instructions and current clinical procedure.

steps.title: Document
steps.instruction: Record and respond to the result.
steps.explanation: Document the reading and follow the relevant escalation or treatment pathway when indicated.

items.title: Wound Dressing
items.description: Learn the structured approach to wound assessment and dressing care.
items.overview: Wound dressing involves assessment, appropriate preparation and application of the selected dressing.
items.why: Consistent wound care supports healing and helps identify complications early.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Assess
steps.instruction: Assess the wound and surrounding skin.
steps.explanation: Observe relevant wound characteristics and compare with previous documentation where available.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Maintain the required infection-prevention and aseptic measures for the procedure.

steps.title: Dress
steps.instruction: Clean and dress the wound as indicated.
steps.explanation: Use the prescribed or approved wound-care technique and dressing.

steps.title: Document
steps.explanation: Record the wound assessment, care provided and patient's response.

items.title: Urinary Catheter Care
items.description: Learn essential principles of caring for a patient with an indwelling urinary catheter.
items.overview: Urinary catheter care aims to maintain a closed system and reduce preventable complications.
items.why: Appropriate catheter care supports patient comfort and infection prevention.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Assess
steps.instruction: Assess the catheter system and patient.
steps.explanation: Check comfort, drainage and the integrity of the catheter system.

steps.title: Maintain
steps.explanation: Keep the system secure and follow current infection-prevention guidance.

steps.title: Provide Care
steps.explanation: Use the approved technique and avoid unnecessary manipulation of the system.

steps.title: Document
steps.explanation: Record relevant findings, urine output when required and any concerns.

items.title: Nasogastric Tube Feeding
items.description: Review the nursing principles involved in enteral feeding through an NG tube.
items.overview: Nasogastric feeding delivers prescribed nutrition or fluids through a feeding tube.
items.why: Safe enteral feeding requires appropriate patient assessment, tube verification and monitoring.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Assess
steps.explanation: Check the patient's condition and follow the current enteral-feeding protocol.

steps.title: Verify
steps.instruction: Verify tube placement using the approved method.
steps.explanation: Do not proceed until tube placement has been confirmed according to current clinical guidance.

steps.title: Feed
steps.explanation: Use the prescribed method, rate and precautions for the patient.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.explanation: Observe for complications and record the feed, flushes and patient response as required.

items.title: Peripheral IV Site Assessment
items.description: Learn how to assess a peripheral IV site for common complications.
items.overview: Peripheral IV site assessment checks the insertion site and surrounding tissue for complications.
items.why: Early recognition of infiltration, phlebitis or other complications supports patient safety.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Inspect
steps.explanation: Look for changes such as redness, swelling, leakage or other abnormal findings.

steps.title: Assess
steps.explanation: Ask about pain or discomfort and assess the site according to local policy.

steps.title: Check
steps.instruction: Check the IV system as required.
steps.explanation: Review patency and the prescribed infusion without unnecessary manipulation.

steps.title: Act
steps.explanation: Follow local escalation and device-management guidance when abnormalities are identified.

items.title: Urine Specimen Collection
items.description: Learn the basic principles of collecting and labelling a urine specimen.
items.overview: Urine specimen collection obtains a sample for laboratory or point-of-care testing.
items.why: Correct collection and labelling help maintain specimen quality and patient safety.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Identify
steps.instruction: Confirm the patient and required specimen.
steps.explanation: Use the approved patient-identification process and check the test requested.

steps.title: Collect
steps.instruction: Collect the specimen using the required method.
steps.explanation: Use the collection method specified for the requested test.

steps.title: Label
steps.explanation: Follow local specimen-labelling requirements before transport.

steps.title: Send
steps.explanation: Follow the laboratory's current handling and transport requirements.

items.title: Oral Care
items.description: Learn a structured approach to oral hygiene for dependent patients.
items.overview: Oral care maintains oral cleanliness, comfort and tissue health.
items.why: Regular oral care supports comfort and can reduce avoidable oral complications.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Assess
steps.explanation: Observe the mouth, lips, teeth, tongue and relevant symptoms before care.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Position the patient safely and explain the procedure.

steps.title: Clean
steps.instruction: Provide oral hygiene using the appropriate technique.
steps.explanation: Clean the mouth gently according to the patient's needs and current clinical guidance.

steps.title: Finish
steps.instruction: Reassess comfort and document as required.
steps.explanation: Ensure the patient is comfortable and record relevant findings or care provided.

items.title: Safe Patient Transfer
items.description: Learn the safety principles for transferring a patient between surfaces.
items.overview: Safe patient transfer uses assessment, appropriate equipment and coordinated movement.
items.why: Good transfer technique reduces avoidable injury risk for patients and staff.
precautions: Escalate unexpected or concerning findings through the appropriate clinical pathway.

steps.title: Assess
steps.explanation: Consider the patient's condition, strength, cognition and required assistance.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.explanation: Position equipment safely and remove avoidable environmental hazards.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.instruction: Perform the transfer with appropriate assistance.
steps.explanation: Use the approved technique and equipment for the patient's assessed needs.

steps.title: Reassess
steps.explanation: Ensure the patient is safe, comfortable and positioned appropriately.
